_readme: The far end of the world, reached the way a player reaches it: village, town, cave.
The cave is two warps from where the game starts, so nothing else in this suite would
ever enter it - and a map no scripted session visits is a map whose tiles, spawns and
doors are only ever validated on paper.

Every leg ends against a wall rather than after a counted number of tiles. The last one leans on that hardest: held into the east wall AND upward, the player slides along the wall until the one row that has a gate in it, and walks out through it.

steps.text: the title opens the game now. A --qa-script run points saves at user://qa_saves and empties it at boot, so there is never anything to Continue - and the cursor opens on the row a press will actually do something with, which is New game. Rows: Continue, New game. One press starts the run.
the warden opens the game now - hear her out before anything else
fetch Rook first: the cave road refuses a player travelling alone, because what waits at the end of it is sized for two. South to the well, west to the wall, south to her.

step off Rook's shoulder. Talking to her leaves the player wedged between her and the west wall, where east is blocked by her body - so this is a short DIAGONAL: the up component clears her, and the right component leaves column 1 before it can reach the hollow's door two rows above. A straight hold up would have to stop within a pixel of that door, which is a count nobody should have to keep true.
and now the wall-anchored legs: east to the east wall, then south onto the road out of the village
down to the south wall, east to the east wall
now up along that wall, still pushing east: the gate is the row that gives
and it is a real place: standing here does not send us back
and back out the same way: west into the wall, sliding down to the row that gives
